sources.citation: Vyas, Yogendra D. 1967. A linguistic study of Bhili dialects: a descriptive study of Central and North Bhili. PhD thesis, Gujarat University (guide P. B. Pandit). Part II North Bhili (Dungarpur).
sources.note: 'Stress is not distinctive.' (Phonemics, thesis p. 133) for North Bhili of Dungarpur (= Wagdi area, wagd1238), a neighbouring variety, not adiw1235; introduction p. 2 cites P. B. Pandit's 1952 fieldwork Idar-Dungarpur.

sources.citation: Cain, Bruce D. (comp.). 2013. A Sociolinguistic Profile of Garasia Dialects. SIL Electronic Survey Report 2013-014. Dallas: SIL International. iii+50 pp.
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey (lexical similarity, recorded-text testing, bilingualism, language attitudes) of Rajput Garasia, Adiwasi Garasia (Bordiyala-Danta, Kadzavas-Poshina/Khedbrahma) and 'Dungari Garasia' of Bhiloda; no phonology; annotated bibliography lists no linguistic description of Garasia.

sources.citation: Acharya, Shantibhai. 1967. Gujarati-Bhili vatchit (Garasiya svarup) [Gujarati-Bhili conversation, Garasiya form]. Ahmedabad: Gujarat Vidyapith. (Gujarati)
sources.note: Nothing. 'Pustika vishe' pp. 7-9 gives pronunciation notes for Gujarati users (i/ii and u/uu contrastive, open e/o, aspirate correspondences, c/ch > s, j, retroflex d, s, loss of initial h) but no remark on stress/svarbhar. Read visually from page scan (Gujarati, no usable scanned).

sources.citation: Acharya, Shantibhai. 1965. Bhili-Gujarati shabdavali: Bhilina (Garasiya boline name janiti) ek svarupni shabdavali [Bhili-Gujarati vocabulary of the form of Bhili known as the Garasiya dialect]. Ahmedabad: Gujarat Vidyapith. (Gujarati; foreword H. C. Bhayani; data from Meghraj-Bhiloda area, Sabarkantha)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction 'Shabdavali jota pahela' pp. 13-15 explains the broad transcription: vowels (high/low i and u, open e/o), consonants (c, j, retroflex d, s, de-aspiration/devoicing of voiced aspirates, loss of nasalisation, loss of initial h); no stress statement. p. 10 reviews earlier work (Thompson 1895, Grierson 1907, Jungblut, N. Jain 1962/1964, T. N. Dave 1943-48, P. B. Pandit 1952).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. (ed.) 1907. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX, Part III: The Bhil languages. Calcutta. Section 'Girasia or Nyar' (Nyar-ki-boli of Marwar/Sirohi = Girasia), with two specimens (Jodhpur, Sirohi).
sources.note: Nothing on accent. Notes only frequent e for other vowels ('dhen', 'kere-ne'; 'in words such as huselo.. the e is probably short'), dental l for cerebral l, genitive -ro, future paradigm; 'agrees with the Bhili of Mahikantha with an admixture of Marwari'. Whole-volume a full-text search for stress/accent finds no Bhili accent statement (only the transcription convention that an acute marks an accented syllable).

sources.citation: Thompson, Charles S. 1895. Rudiments of the Bhili language. Ahmedabad: United Printing Press. (CMS mission, Bhili of Mahikantha/Kherwara-Lusadia)
sources.access_detail: a digital copy (available on request); access check: open copy online; also held in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number 3254.104)
sources.note: Preface p. ii-iii: 'The tone and the accent are not quite the same in places separated by, say, a score of miles' and the Kotra dialect's partiality for e; no statement of where accent falls; 'no accents have been placed over the long vowels' (typographic).
